Traupman 300

adhūc

up to now, as yet, still

Strictly “up to this point”: what has been so until now. With a negative it is “not yet” (adhūc nōn, or nōndum). In a question like “are you still awake?” Latin uses etiam: Etiam vigilās?.

Other words

  • hāctenus — so far, thus far

    also used · classical · Traupman 313

Examples

  • itaque nēmō adhūc convenīre mē voluit, cui fuerim occupātus

    and so no one who has wanted to see me has yet found me tied upCic. Sen. 32

  • Etiam vigilās? — Vigilō.

    Are you awake yet? — I amPlaut. Most. 383, 373b

See also not yet, so far so good, already, be awake.
